reasoning: Identity and page check pass at 53 FR 30639 (Executive Order 12649 of August 11, 1988, Offsets in Military-Related Exports). The single strike-and-insert command replacing section 602(d)(2) of EO 10480 (text that EO 12521 had added) is the whole operative text, and the one-clause inventory covers it. EO 12919 section 904(a) states that the listed orders 'are superseded or revoked' and item (10) names EO 12649; EO 12919 has no effective-date wording, so the signing date of 1994-06-03 is the first end, and the claim correctly says this is a reading of the text. The genuine claim gives 1994-06-03 in first_end, whole_order_end and judgment_reason, so the dates agree. The held texts show no earlier revocation or supersession: EO 10480 itself is revoked on the same day by section 904(a)(3). The savings statement is accurate. Section 401 reassigns the offsets function to Commerce as a command of the later order, collection already done is accrued, and section 903 keeps prior actions in effect only where they are consistent with the new order. It does not continue EO 12649, which section 904 revokes by name. The searches are described honestly. Not counted as a defect: the claim does not mention the 1990-91 lapse of the Defense Production Act. No statute text for that lapse is held, and a lapse would at most suspend the order, not end it.
